title: Node profile contracts: GPU ABI labeling and heartbeat signal spec
content:
Purpose:
This note proposes a contract-first model for node profiles that decouples routing decisions from volatile telemetry while giving the control plane a compact, stable view of fleet capabilities. It standardizes: (1) a GPU ABI/compatibility label namespace, (2) an immutable node capability profile, and (3) a smoothed set of health signals and a health-score used by routing filters and regional failover logic.

Scope:
- Applies to all inference-serving node classes (hosted + dedicated + on-prem variants).
- Excludes scheduling internals of upstream cloud providers; focuses on the inventory/control-plane surface and discovery API.

Goals:
- Make capability matching deterministic for routing (avoid chalky ad-hoc tag parsing across services).
- Provide a compact node-profile contract for model-compatibility checks (quantization, kernel selection).
- Normalize health signals so routing decisions don’t flip-flop on transient spikes.
- Support eventual consistency across regions with deterministic rollback/fallback.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Inventory updates can be eventually consistent (AP model), but routing needs bounded staleness guarantees (max 30s view allowed for last-known-good on a node).
- GPU driver ABI mismatches are the most common cause of runtime failure for compiled kernels; labeling must include driver + CUDA/rocm ABI hints.
- Telemetry ingestion is resource constrained; health signals must be compact and sparse by default.

High-level model:
1) NodeProfile (immutable-ish metadata): a small set of capability attributes that only change on node reprovision or driver upgrade. These are authoritative for routing compatibility checks.
2) HealthStream (time-series): frequent telemetry (heartbeat, gpu_util, mem_free, temp, ecc_errors) used to compute HealthScore. The HealthScore is what routing and autoscaler consult — not raw telemetry.
3) Inventory API: exposes NodeProfile + lastHealthScore + lastSeenTimestamp + regionalPlacement.

NodeProfile schema (contract):
- node_id: stable UUID assigned by control plane
- infra_class: ["dedicated-gpu", "shared-gpu", "baremetal"]
- compute_tier: ["cpu-only", "gpu-legacy", "gpu-accelerated"]
- gpu_family: short string (e.g., "h100", "a100", "rtx6000")
- gpu_mem_gb: integer (GB)
- gpu_abi: comma-separated tokens describing runtime compatibility. Example tokens: "cuda11-8-cuobjdump-v2", "nvfuser-compat-1", "rocm5-3-abi"
- driver_hash: short hash of installed driver/kernel combo
- acceleration_features: list of features exposed (examples: "fp16-mixed", "int8-quant", "sparse-kernel")
- network_zone: region/zone tag (e.g., "us-west1-a")
- immutable_profile_version: semver-like string incremented on reprovision
- labels: free-form map converted to flat list for discovery (see label rules)

Labeling rules and recommended keys (kept small):
- rd:role - routing role (values: inference, batch, egress)
- rd:gpu_family - normalized family (h100, a100, a10, t4)
- rd:quant_profile - recommended quantization (none, 8-bit, 4-bit)
- rd:owner - product/team owning node pool
- rd:cost_tier - {spot, reserved, premium}
Notes: prefix labels with "rd:" to avoid collisions and make discovery cheap. Keep values short.

GPU ABI and compatibility approach:
Problem: minor driver or runtime variation can require different compiled kernels. We introduce a GPU ABI token set on NodeProfile (gpu_abi). Routing and kernel selection use set-subset checks: a model variant advertises a minimal gpu_abi set; a node profile must be a superset to be considered compatible.
Example: model X (requires) ["cuda11-8-cuobjdump-v2","nvfuser-compat-1"]
Node A (provides) ["cuda11-7","nvfuser-compat-1"] => incompatible (missing cuda11-8 token).
Node B (provides) ["cuda11-8-cuobjdump-v2","nvfuser-compat-1","cublas-2.2"] => compatible.

Health signals and normalization:
- Raw signals ingested (per-node): heartbeat, gpu_util_pct, gpu_mem_available_mb, temperature_c, ecc_count, process_exit_rate, queue_depth, io_latency_ms
- Sampling cadence: default 10s; can be relaxed to 30s for low-priority pools.
- Smoothing: every raw metric is decayed with exponential moving average (alpha configurable, default alpha=0.2). Instant anomalies are captured separately (see incident flag below).
- HealthScore: integer 0..100 computed every evaluation window (default 3 samples). Baseline 100; penalties applied for thresholds exceeded.

HealthScore pseudo-formula: (kept intentionally simple)
HealthScore = clamp(0,100, 100 - util_penalty - temp_penalty - mem_penalty - ecc_penalty - queue_penalty - flapping_penalty)
Where util_penalty = max(0, (ema_gpu_util - 80) * 0.5)
temp_penalty = max(0, (ema_temp_c - 82) * 1.0)
mem_penalty = 20 if ema_mem_available_mb < 1024 else 0
ecc_penalty = min(50, ecc_count * 10)
queue_penalty = min(40, queue_depth * 5)
flapping_penalty = 30 if node marked as "flapping" (see logic)

Flapping detection and incident flags:
- Flapping: node health toggles across threshold more than 3 times in 2 minutes => set flapping flag for 15 minutes. Flapping sets a large temporary penalty and keeps node out of high-availability routing.
- Incident flag: critical non-recoverable (driver crash on boot, repeated kernel timeouts). Set by SRE/agent and triggers immediate scale/fallback. Incidents must be human-reviewed.

Routing decision flow (stateless filter pipeline):
1) Capability filter: match NodeProfile against request requirements (gpu_abi subset, gpu_family, gpu_mem)
2) Cost and policy filter: remove nodes that violate policy (cost_tier, owner, region restrictions)
3) Health filter: only nodes with HealthScore >= configured threshold (defaults: 70 for production, 40 for batch)
4) Rank/selection: sort by score = w1*HealthScore + w2*proximity_score - w3*estimated_cost
5) Final circuit-breaker: if selected node has lastSeenTimestamp > allowed staleness => fallback to alternative pool

Multi-region inventory considerations:
- Each region runs an independent inventory writer; a globally federated read model is maintained by streaming deltas to the global control plane.
- Use compact delta stream: node profile changes and health score deltas only (no full state dumps).
- Convergence model: optimistic replication with vector clocks on NodeProfile immutable_version. Conflicts resolved in control-plane: prefer higher immutable_profile_version, then lower driver_hash lexicographically as tiebreaker.
- Regional failover: routing policies must embed locality preferences and a global fallback policy. On region outage, control plane must decrease locality_weight for that region gradually and route to next region, but only to nodes whose gpu_abi is compatible.

Inventory API sketch (read-only surface for routers):
GET /v1/inventory/nodes?filters=... => returns list of NodeProfile + lastHealthScore + lastSeenTimestamp (JSON compact rows)
GET /v1/inventory/nodes/{node_id} => NodeProfile + extended telemetry windows
POST /v1/inventory/announce -> used by node agent to register (idempotent)
/healthstream publishes compressed time-series to internal kafka topic for scorer service.

Operational notes and rollout plan:
- Phase 1: implement NodeProfile + read API and use-only in a single low-risk fleet (batch-inference). Run for 4 weeks.
- Phase 2: enable HealthScore-based filtering for non-critical routes (A/B test with 10% traffic). Tune penalties.
- Phase 3: enable ABI-superset checks for new model rollout to prevent kernel-mismatch failures.
- Phase 4: multi-region delta streaming and global read model; deprecate ad-hoc label parsing across services.

Migration and compatibility strategies:
- Backfill: inventory service will compute gpu_abi tokens from existing driver metadata using heuristics, mark as "inferred" and send to teams to verify.
- Compatibility shim: routers can operate in "permissive" mode (ignore ABI mismatch) for rollout until the fleet is stabilized.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Token vocabulary governance: who owns token registry? propose "platform-component" as owner and a small RFC process for adding tokens.
- Should immutable_profile_version be globally incrementing or node-local counter? Current proposal: node-local semver to indicate reprovision cycles. Control plane resolves by timestamp/clock when needed.
- How to model accelerator features that are not GPU (e.g., Habana, AWS-triton accelerators)? Proposal: extend gpu_family -> accel_family generic name and use feature tokens.

Action items:
- [Aisha] Draft registry of initial gpu_abi tokens and publish to confluence (due 2024-09-05)
- [Marco] Prototype healthscore scorer as a standalone service (kafka consumer) (due 2024-10-01)
- [Diego] Add permissive ABI check flag to router (feature flag) and run smoke tests (due 2024-09-20)

Appendix: Example NodeProfile (compact JSON row representation):
{"node_id":"9b3c-...","infra_class":"dedicated-gpu","compute_tier":"gpu-accelerated","gpu_family":"a100","gpu_mem_gb":"80","gpu_abi":"cuda11-8-cuobjdump-v2,nvfuser-compat-1","driver_hash":"d4f2a1","acceleration_features":"fp16-mixed,int8-quant","network_zone":"us-west1-a","immutable_profile_version":"1.2.0","labels":"rd:role=inference,rd:cost_tier=reserved,rd:owner=vision-team"}

Notes: This doc is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight — it aims to give the routing and serving teams a stable contract to code against while allowing ops to iterate on scoring. Feedback welcome.
